name: Kadhi Pakora
cuisine: North Indian (Punjabi; also cooked across Rajasthan, Haryana, UP and Delhi; on most Punjabi and homestyle menus in Mumbai)

ingredients.name: Onion (pyaz/kanda)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ medium onion, thinly sliced (about ⅓ cup slices)

ingredients.name: Sunflower oil (or other neutral oil), for deep-frying

equipment: Mixing bowl and a whisk (no whisk? a fork works; a small hand blender gives the smoothest base)
Heavy-bottomed saucepan, about 1.5 litres, for the kadhi (it froths up when it boils, so do not use a tiny pan)
Small kadai for deep-frying, with a slotted spoon (jhara)
Tadka pan or a small steel ladle (no tadka pan? use the smallest pan you have)
Plate lined with kitchen paper, for draining the pakoras
Knife, chopping board, grater (for the ginger)
Measuring spoons and a measuring cup (a normal teaspoon and a steel glass are fine stand-ins)

steps.title: Whisk the curd
steps.text: Put 100 g sour curd in the mixing bowl and whisk until completely smooth.
steps.visualCue: No lumps, glossy and pourable
steps.cameraCheck: The smooth curd in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Whisk beating curd in a bowl.

steps.title: Add besan and spices to the curd
steps.text: Add 1½ tbsp (12 g) besan, a pinch (0.3 g) turmeric and ¼ tsp (0.5 g) Kashmiri chilli powder. Whisk to a smooth paste.
steps.tip: Mix besan into the curd before the water; lumps are much harder to remove later. Do not add salt yet (FitPlate adds it after the boil, step 14).
steps.visualCue: Even yellow paste, no dry flour specks
steps.cameraCheck: The yellow paste on the whisk
steps.videoShot: Besan sprinkled in and whisked smooth.

steps.title: Add the water
steps.text: Pour in 250 ml (1 cup) water a little at a time, whisking.
steps.visualCue: Thin, buttermilk-like liquid, pale yellow
steps.videoShot: Water poured in while whisking.

steps.title: Slice the onion
steps.text: Thinly slice ¼ medium onion (30 g) and separate the layers.
steps.visualCue: Thin half-moon slices, about ⅓ cup
steps.videoShot: Knife slicing onion thinly.

steps.title: Chop the pakora greens
steps.text: Finely chop ½ small green chilli (1 g) and 1 tsp coriander leaves (2 g). Grate ½-inch ginger (3 g) for the kadhi and slit the other ½ green chilli; keep these aside separately.
steps.visualCue: Small green bits; grated ginger in a little heap
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped chilli-coriander and the grated ginger
steps.videoShot: Coriander chopped, ginger grated.

steps.title: Mix the pakora batter (dry)
steps.text: In a small bowl combine 3 tbsp (25 g) besan, a pinch of ajwain (crushed between your palms), a pinch each of chilli powder and turmeric, a pinch (0.5 g) salt, the onion, chopped chilli and coriander. Squeeze the onion into the flour and rest 10 min.
steps.tip: Salt pulls water out of the onion, so you need very little extra water.
steps.visualCue: Onion slices coated in flour, looking damp after resting
steps.videoShot: Hands rubbing onion into besan.

steps.title: Heat the frying oil
steps.text: Heat about 150 ml oil in the small kadai on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: A drop of batter sinks briefly, then rises with steady bubbles (not smoking)
steps.cameraCheck: The test drop rising in the oil
steps.videoShot: A drop of batter sizzling up.

steps.title: Finish the batter
steps.text: Add water 1 tsp at a time (about 1 tbsp in all) and mix to a thick, sticky batter.
steps.tip: Too thin and the pakoras soak up oil and break in the kadhi; too thick and they stay hard.
steps.visualCue: Batter holds the onion together and drops off a spoon in a blob, not a stream
steps.cameraCheck: A spoonful of batter held up
steps.videoShot: Batter falling from a spoon in a lump.

steps.title: Fry the pakoras
steps.text: Drop 4 small portions of batter (about 1 heaped tbsp each) into the oil and fry on medium, turning a few times.
steps.tip: On high heat the outside browns while the inside stays raw; keep it medium.
steps.visualCue: Deep golden-brown, crisp, bubbles slowing down
steps.cameraCheck: The golden pakoras in the oil
steps.videoShot: Pakoras turned with a slotted spoon.

steps.title: Drain the pakoras
steps.text: Lift them out onto the paper-lined plate. Turn off the frying oil (cool and keep it for reuse).
steps.visualCue: Crisp, golden, oil draining onto the paper
steps.videoShot: Pakoras placed on kitchen paper.

steps.title: Start the kadhi
steps.text: Pour the kadhi mix into the heavy saucepan, add the grated ginger and slit chilli, and put it on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: Pale yellow liquid in the pan
steps.cameraCheck: The pan with the kadhi mix
steps.videoShot: Kadhi mix poured into the pan.

steps.title: Stir to the boil
steps.text: Stir continuously until it comes to a full boil.
steps.tip: This is the step where kadhi splits. Keep stirring and keep the heat medium; once it has boiled, it is safe.
steps.visualCue: It froths and rises once, then bubbles; smooth, no grainy white bits
steps.videoShot: Spoon stirring as the kadhi foams up.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Lower the heat and simmer uncovered, stirring every 2–3 min.
steps.tip: Too thick? Add 2–3 tbsp hot water. Most sources simmer 15–25 min; longer gives a deeper flavour.
steps.visualCue: Thickens to coat the back of a spoon; the raw besan smell is gone; a little oil shine on top
steps.videoShot: Finger drawn across a coated spoon leaves a clear line.

steps.title: Add the salt
steps.text: Stir in ¼ tsp (1.5 g) salt.
steps.visualCue: Salt dissolved
steps.videoShot: Salt sprinkled over the kadhi.

steps.title: Add the pakoras
steps.text: Slide the 4 pakoras into the kadhi and simmer on low.
steps.tip: Want them softer? Leave them 10 min off the heat in the kadhi before serving.
steps.visualCue: Pakoras swell a little and soften at the edges, but hold their shape
steps.videoShot: Pakoras dropped into the bubbling kadhi.

steps.title: Heat the tadka oil
steps.text: Heat 1 tsp (5 g) oil (or ghee) in the tadka pan on medium.
steps.visualCue: Oil shimmers
steps.cameraCheck: The oil in the tadka pan
steps.videoShot: Oil swirling in a small pan.

steps.title: Crackle the mustard
steps.text: Add ⅛ tsp (0.5 g) mustard seeds.
steps.visualCue: Seeds pop and jump
steps.videoShot: Mustard seeds crackling.

steps.title: Add cumin, methi and red chilli
steps.text: Add ¼ tsp cumin, 8–10 fenugreek seeds and 1 dried red chilli.
steps.tip: Black methi seeds make the kadhi bitter; take it off the heat as soon as they are golden.
steps.visualCue: Cumin sizzles; methi seeds turn light golden; chilli darkens slightly
steps.videoShot: Spices sizzling in the ladle.

steps.title: Add hing and chilli powder, then pour
steps.text: Turn off the heat, add a pinch of hing and a pinch of Kashmiri chilli powder, swirl once and pour the tadka over the kadhi at once.
steps.visualCue: Bright red oil spreads over the yellow kadhi with a loud sizzle
steps.cameraCheck: The red tadka on the kadhi
steps.videoShot: Tadka poured over the kadhi, sizzling.

steps.title: Taste and adjust
steps.text: Stir, taste and adjust: a pinch of salt, or ½ tsp lemon juice if the curd was not sour enough.
steps.visualCue: Tangy, mildly spicy, no raw flour taste
steps.videoShot: A spoonful lifted for tasting.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Ladle into a bowl with the pakoras on top and serve hot.
steps.visualCue: Thick, pale-yellow kadhi with red tadka streaks and golden pakoras
steps.videoShot: Steam rising from the bowl next to a plate of rice.

reasons: a fair amount of plant protein and folate from 37 g besan, calcium and B12 from curd, no added sugar and little saturated fat (about 3.7 g), at about 345 kcal. Points off for the deep-fried pakoras (about a third of the calories come from oil), moderate sodium (about 860 mg) and almost no vegetables, so very little vitamin C or A. Restaurant versions usually fry more and bigger pakoras, often add ghee or butter to the tadka and more salt, so 450–550 kcal bowls with more saturated fat are likely (est.).

researchRating.basis: a much-loved North Indian comfort dish ("kadhi chawal" has its own Wikipedia article); Hebbar's Kitchen's Punjabi kadhi pakoda shows 4.99 from 336 votes (plus 5.0 from 186 on its Hindi page), Archana's Kitchen's version shows about 6,600 ratings, Cooking and Me's recipe has a comment thread of about 100 comments, and almost every major Indian recipe site (Veg Recipes of India, Tarla Dalal, Ranveer Brar, Indian Healthy Recipes, Spice Up The Curry) publishes it. Points off because it splits easily for beginners, the pakoras are fried, and it is often seen as homely rather than a restaurant favourite. Platform dish ratings were not used.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 2 days (cool within 1 hour); the kadhi thickens and the pakoras turn very soft. Freezer: not recommended, as curd-based kadhi tends to split on thawing and the pakoras go mushy; if you cook in a batch, freeze or keep the fried pakoras separately and add them to fresh kadhi. Reheat on low heat with 2–4 tbsp water, stirring, until it just bubbles; do not boil hard. Microwave in 1-minute bursts, stirring between.
leftoverRemix: Kadhi pakoda khichdi. Cook 3 tbsp rice with 1 tbsp moong dal and a pinch of turmeric into a soft khichdi, then stir in the leftover kadhi and break up the pakoras into it; finish with a fresh cumin-and-red-chilli tadka. (Khichdi Bar sells a "Punjabi Kadhi Pakoda Khichdi" in this style.)
burnOff: about 4.9 km of running (345 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 6.9 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 25 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With ¾ cup rice (about 500 kcal): about 7.1 km running or 10 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: besan, onion, hing and table salt are outside the common vrat rule set; make the kadhi with rajgira (amaranth) flour and sendha namak, skip the pakoras and hing (see Navratri vrat variant).

ekadashi.reason: besan is a pulse (chickpea), avoided with grains in the common rule set; the same rajgira vrat kadhi works (family rules on spices vary).

jain.reason: onion and fresh ginger are root vegetables; use methi-leaf pakoras and sonth (Jain variant).

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; with rice it is a filling iftar or dinner; it is fried and fairly salty (about 860 mg sodium), so go easy at sehri.

jain.reason: onion (in the pakoras) and fresh ginger are root vegetables; swap onion for methi leaves and ginger for dry ginger powder (sonth) (see Jain variant). Hing and the other spices are fine.

vegan.reason: use unsweetened cashew or other plant yogurt instead of curd and oil instead of ghee (see Vegan variant).

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat, so it fits a pescatarian diet.

sattvik.reason: the main recipe has no garlic; skip the onion in the pakoras and make plain ajwain pakoras (see Sattvik variant).

glutenFree.reason: besan (chickpea flour) is gluten-free, but the tadka uses hing, and most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour; use gluten-free hing or skip it.

dairyFree.reason: curd is the base; use plant yogurt (same swap as the Vegan variant).
